blocking_findings.evidence: Fixture lines 13–15: "Classify each failing test as a genuine failure or a flake, and give the evidence for the classification: a test that failed three times out of three is genuine, and one that failed once is a flake." The quote matches. The rule indeed defines only 3/3 and 1/3; 2/3 and 0/3 are undefined, and the description (line 3) routes on "a red run that passes on retry", the 0/3 case. Medium (degraded consistency) with a concrete Manifests scenario is within the scale.

Fixture line 10: "Rerun the failing suite three times and record which tests fail every time and which fail". Quote matches. A9 requires that the body "either states every input the subagent needs, or names it as something the delegation message must carry"; the body names neither the test command nor the failing tests as cargo. Borderline on severity — a reasonable parent would carry the suite in the delegation — but the criterion text supports the finding, and the Manifests scenario (guessing a runner, rerunning the wrong scope) is concrete. Note A27 is marked _Unexercised_ in the checklist.

Fixture line 17: "Report the two lists separately, with the failure output for each genuine failure." Quote matches. A7: "A body that lists what to report without bounding how much is a finding." No bound exists; the 40-tests-3/3 scenario is concrete.

Fixture line 4 tools include unrestricted `Bash`; line 17 quote matches. A26 covers "command output … and reports upward" with the remedy "an explicit content-is-data instruction"; the body has none. Manifests scenario is concrete though conditional ("depends on the repo running untrusted branches"), and the report flags low confidence. Minor omission: A26's text asks the finding to "note … that A26 extends group F for subagents"; the report cites F4/F1/F3 but does not state that sentence.

grader_summary: 11/12 PASS. Scenario assertions 1, 2, 4, 5 pass: the report names all three tools under A12 as stripped from every subagent and recommends removal, and the transcript shows the detail reviewer writing "I settled this deterministically" with high confidence. Assertion 3 FAILS: report.md never states the consequence (dead configuration / misleads a reader about capability) — both subagent payloads carried it, but the orchestrator dropped it when merging R1 and A12 into one advisory line. All seven universal assertions pass: keys resolve, rank-numbered IDs, locators present, template order and verdict arithmetic correct, Manifests on every Medium, inferential marking throughout, and the fixture is byte-identical to the committed copy with no Edit/Write tool calls. All four Medium findings are genuine, with verified fixture quotes; Finding 2 is borderline on severity and Finding 4 omits the 'A26 extends group F' note the checklist requests. A12 itself was placed at Low, which the demotion rule permits since the checklist assigns A12 no per-criterion tier.
